title: Monetary Policy and Economic Developments - Federal Reserve
summary: This Federal Reserve Annual Report chapter reviews U.S. monetary policy and economic developments in 2018, a period when the FOMC raised the federal funds target range twice to reach 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent. The labor market strengthened with payrolls averaging 224,000/month and unemployment near 4 percent, while inflation moderated to 1.7 percent (PCE) by December 2018. The FOMC signaled patience at its January 2019 meeting amid late-2018 financial market volatility and softer global conditions.
key_points: FOMC raised target range for federal funds rate twice in H2 2018, reaching 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent by December
January 2019 FOMC meeting indicated patience in determining future rate adjustments amid softer global conditions
Labor market strengthened with payroll employment averaging 224,000/month since June 2018; unemployment ~4 percent
Inflation (PCE) declined to 1.7 percent in December 2018 from above 2 percent mid-year; core inflation 1.9 percent
Financial conditions tightened markedly from early October to late December 2018 with heightened volatility
Foreign economic growth stepped down significantly in 2018, particularly in euro area; China slowdown notable
U.S. financial system described as substantially more resilient than pre-crisis decade with high capital ratios
why_it_matters: This historical document provides context on 2018 Fed policy trajectory when rates were being gradually raised toward 2.25-2.50 percent. The shift to 'patient' guidance at January 2019 marked a significant pivot point. While stale for forward-looking analysis, it documents the economic and financial conditions (late-2018 volatility, global slowdown) that preceded the Fed's 2019 policy reversal.
macro_context: Documents 2018 economic conditions: GDP growth ~3 percent for full year, consumer spending strong early but weakening toward year-end, business investment growth slowed from H1, housing activity declined on rising rates. Foreign growth notably slowed; dollar strengthened slightly. Core inflation at 1.9 percent remains near but below 2 percent target. The 2018 monetary policy path of gradual removal of accommodation was reversed in 2019 as conditions softened.
important_numbers: 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent (federal funds target range by December 2018)
